references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 12:43-44|Mark 12:43-44] tells the same story about the widow's offering, where Jesus explains that she gave more than all the others because she gave out of her poverty – everything she had to live on.

[ref:2 Cor 8:2-3|2 Corinthians 8:2-3] describes the churches in Macedonia who gave generously out of their deep poverty, beyond their ability, and voluntarily – the same principle of giving from what they lacked rather than from their abundance.

[ref:2 Cor 8:12|2 Corinthians 8:12] emphasizes that generosity is judged by what one has, not by what one does not have – God looks at the willingness of the heart and the readiness to give, as the widow showed.
[ref:Deut 24:17|Deuteronomy 24:17] shows God's care for widows and vulnerable people, which forms the background for Jesus' attention to this poor widow.
[ref:Prov 11:24|Proverbs 11:24] says that those who give freely will receive even more, while those who hold back will suffer lack – the widow gave away everything she had.

[ref:1 John 3:17|1 John 3:17] speaks of giving from what one has to someone in need, and asks how God's love can remain in anyone who closes their heart – the widow's offering shows such radical love in action.
[ref:Phil 4:11-12|Philippians 4:11-12] is about living in abundance and in lack. Paul learned to be content in any situation, just as the widow showed trust in God even in her poverty.

The preceding verses in [ref:Luke 21:1-3|Luke 21:1-3] provide the immediate context: Jesus sees the rich putting their gifts into the temple treasury and says that this poor widow gave more than all the others.

[ref:1 Kings 17:8-16|1 Kings 17:8-16] tells of the widow in Zarephath who gave Elijah the last bit of food she had, and then experienced God's miraculous provision – an Old Testament parallel to the widow's radical willingness to give.
